title: Shopify Overexposed Scans GKE Ingresses and Cloud Run for Exposure
gist: Shopify rebuilt its Overexposed scanner for unauthenticated GKE Ingresses and Cloud Run services after a repo-config-based version produced false positives and blind spots; the new design uses GCP Cloud Asset Inventory plus a single anonymous HTTP probe and six evidence-backed verdicts, cutting inconclusive Ingress verdicts by ~80%. The piece frames a general split between rule/config-based scanners (intent) and inventory-based ones (enforcement).

themes.theme: Config shows intent, cluster shows enforcement

insights.claim: Shopify's first exposure scanner, which read Ingress configs from its infrastructure repository, failed because proxy-auth annotations caused false positives, admission controllers that rewrite settings didn't run in every cluster, and Ingresses created by other repos or platform tooling were never seen.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Repository-based security scanning systematically misses runtime reality, a gap security tooling vendors can exploit.
insights.locator: The original scanner checked the infrastructure repository

insights.claim: Shopify's lesson for cloud security scanning is that the repository shows intent while the cluster shows what is actually enforced.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Security posture tools grounded in live cloud inventory have an edge over shift-left config scanners alone.
insights.quote: the repository shows intent; the cluster shows what is enforced
insights.locator: The original scanner checked the infrastructure repository

insights.claim: Rebuilding the scanner on GCP Cloud Asset Inventory and an anonymous HTTP probe reduced inconclusive Ingress verdicts by about 80% within a few weeks of tuning.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Inventory-plus-probe approaches materially improve signal quality in exposure management.
insights.quote: this reduced inconclusive Ingress verdicts by around 80%

insights.claim: Querying Cloud Asset Inventory surfaced Cloud Run services in GCP projects that Shopify's first scanner had never covered at all.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Shadow cloud assets are common even at sophisticated companies, sustaining demand for asset discovery tools.

insights.claim: In early runs of the rebuilt scanner, roughly three in four results were inconclusive in one July run before the team grouped results by reason and added evidence-backed verdicts.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Exposure scanning without careful verdict design produces mostly noise.
insights.locator: In early runs, roughly three in four

insights.claim: Shopify's Overexposed maps each anonymous probe to one of six verdicts—exposed, expected, protected, not found, unreachable and inconclusive—and treats uncertain evidence as inconclusive rather than defaulting to protected.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Defaulting to 'unknown' instead of 'safe' is a design principle that reduces false assurance in security tooling.
insights.quote: Uncertain evidence stays inconclusive rather than defaulting to protected.
insights.locator: In early runs, roughly three in four

insights.claim: HTTP status codes are context-dependent for exposure checks: a Cloud Run 404 may come from Google's front end before the app runs, and a 403 is not treated as proof of protection.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Naive status-code-based scanners can systematically misreport exposure.

insights.claim: For Cloud Run, a service is public only if allUsers holds the invoker role or the invoker check is disabled, so Shopify's scanner distinguishes ingress settings from IAM.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Correct exposure assessment requires modeling both network and identity layers.

insights.claim: Allowlisted endpoints are still probed on every run, and allowlist entries that turn out to be protected or gone are flagged as stale.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Continuous re-validation of exceptions prevents allowlist rot.

themes.theme: Securing the scanner and AI-built tooling

insights.claim: Because the scanner requests arbitrary hostnames, Shopify hardened it against SSRF by validating every DNS-returned IP, rejecting private/loopback addresses, pinning connections to the checked IP to prevent DNS rebinding, and re-checking on each redirect.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Security tools themselves expand attack surface and need egress controls, including metadata endpoints.
insights.locator: Because the scanner makes outbound requests

insights.claim: Shopify built Overexposed using AI coding agents and AI code review, and applied mutation testing to security guards plus one canary target per verdict to catch tests that pass while checking the wrong thing.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: AI-written security code requires stronger verification techniques like mutation testing to be trusted.
insights.locator: The team built Overexposed with AI

insights.claim: Rule-based checks such as Trend Micro's Cloud Run rule are cheap and CI-friendly but report intent rather than enforcement, missing resources created outside the repo and settings rewritten by admission controllers.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Config-only CSPM rules leave blind spots that inventory-based products can address.

insights.claim: Inventory-based tools like Cartography close config blind spots but still derive exposure flags from configuration, so they cannot confirm what an outsider actually sees; adding an anonymous probe fills that gap.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Active external verification is a differentiator in the attack-surface management space.

insights.claim: The recommended design for exposure scanners is to use cloud inventory as the main reference, keep config analysis as an early CI signal, and add a probe only when inventory cannot show whether access control works.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Provides a layered blueprint for enterprise cloud security programs.
insights.quote: use inventory as the main reference. Keep config analysis as an early signal in CI.
